title: promptctl's shallow-edge change index disagrees with git in a PR merge checkout when the two parents' dates fall on different days
problem: test_promptctl.LastChangeIndexTest.test_lookups_without_a_git_call_match_the_per_file_call failed on PR #19525's `validate` job (run 45914295040, 2026-11-27 00:01 UTC) with ' (file last changed on or before 2026-11-27, the shallow-clone edge)' from the index against '... 2026-11-26 ...' from `git log -1 -- .claude/hooks/block_pkill_f.py`. CI checks out refs/pull/N/merge: both parents (base tip and PR head) are shallow roots and each 'adds' every file. _last_change_indexes() keeps the first edge commit in log order (the newest, here the PR head, committed in UTC on 11-27); git follows the TREESAME parent, the first parent (base, committed 16:58-07:00, so dated 11-26 by when[:10]). It shows only when the two committer dates fall on different calendar days in their own timezones, so it looks flaky and appears around midnight. Any PR can hit it; the diff does not matter.
evidence: PR #19525 validate job 140229690133 log: AssertionError, Tuples differ (2026-11-27 vs 2026-11-26), path='.claude/hooks/block_pkill_f.py'
prompts/promptctl.py _last_change_indexes: `into.setdefault(line, cur)` over edge commits in log order
change: Make the edge index follow git: when more than one shallow root lists a path, prefer the root git would walk to (first parent while the merge is TREESAME to it; compare blobs with `git ls-tree` on the roots when they differ), or mark such paths ambiguous so _index_hit returns None and the per-file call answers. Keep the speed: a single-root clone (most sessions) must stay one `git log` pass. Add a test that builds a two-root merge in a temp repo with parents dated on different days.
metric: validate failures of this test on PRs in the 14 days after merge
